articles.title: Virginia senator L Louise Lucas charged over allegations she ran criminal marijuana scheme
articles.summary: Democratic Senator L Louise Lucas and six other people, including her family members, are accused of illegally distributing the drug.
articles.body:
Federal prosecutors arrested a prominent Virginia lawmaker on Thursday over allegations she oversaw a criminal marijuana enterprise.

Democratic state Senator L Louise Lucas and six other people, including her family members, have been charged in relation to a sweeping racketeering case that allegedly involves fraud, drug violations, and bribery.

Lucas, 82, claimed the prosecution was politically motivated in a statement on X.

"I will not be intimidated," she wrote. "I will not be bullied. And I will not back down."

While she has not entered a formal plea, Lucas' attorney, Anthony Capozzolo, told the BBC she would plead not guilty.

Capozollo said in a statement they were "surprised and disheartened" to learn of the indictment, and that Lucas "denies these charges in their entirety."

Lucas and her co-conspirators are charged with obtaining and illegally distributing large amounts of illegal marijuana. The government has also accused her of using her political influence to benefit herself and her family.

Lucas was herself charged with five counts, including racketeering conspiracy, conspiracy to distribute marijuana, conspiracy to launder money, conspiracy to commit honest services fraud, and maintaining a drug involved premises.

Other alleged participants were charged with a firearm charge and wire fraud.

Lucas is not running for re-election. But her daughter Lisa Lucas-Burke, who is also charged in the indictment, is running for the city council of Portsmouth, Virginia.

"I grew up under Jim Crow," Lucas wrote on X in response to the charges, referencing an era of legal segregation in the US. "I've seen what happens when people in power try to silence those who stand up to them. I spent my entire life fighting back, and I'm not stopping now."

At a press conference on Thursday, US Attorney General Todd Blanche accused Lucas of overseeing a criminal "enterprise", arranging for the "acquisition and distribution of marijuana," and using her power as a lawmaker to influence legislation that would benefit herself and her family.

Lucas has served in the Virginia State Senate since 1992, and assumed the powerful role of Senate president pro tempore in 2000. She has publicly spoken about her cannabis dispensary and her support for legalised usage, as well as her opposition to President Donald Trump and Republican lawmakers.

"I'm a 78 year grandma who legalized pot and now has her own cannabis store. And I'm the last thing standing between The GOP and total control of Virginia. That's worth an RT!" she wrote on X in 2022.

While small amounts of cannabis are legal in Virginia for personal or medical use, major restrictions remain in place regarding its sale and consumption.

Lucas has backed legislation to legalise recreational marijuana.

She is an owner of The Cannabis Outlet in Portsmouth, Virginia, which opened in 2021 after the state decriminalised simple marijuana possession and legalised personal possession of certain small amounts of marijuana, according to WAVY News.

The Virginia Mercury reported in 2022 that products sold in her shop may have contained substances and dosages that conflicted with state law at the time.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) raided Lucas' office and a cannabis business in May as part of a long-running inquiry, the Washington Post reported at the time.

It is unusual for the justice department to announce major actions involving lawmakers, candidates, or other electorally sensitive matters in the weeks before an election. Early voting is already under way in the US midterm elections, which are held on 3 November.

However, the justice department has announced a series of inquiries against lawmakers and election officials in recent days, including conducting a raid on the home of Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar as the government investigates her immigration status.

Referring to Lucas' case, Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger, a Democrat, wrote on X: "The timing of this indictment undermines the US Department of Justice's previously longstanding policy of not taking legal actions — to include indictments or significant investigative steps — close to an election."

She added: "And sadly, this timing further erodes the trust the American people deserve to have in the Department of Justice."

articles.title: Don’t blindly follow foreign custody order: Supreme Court
articles.summary: As cases of estranged NRI couples fighting for child custody increasingly result in cross-border litigation, with one spouse getting a favourable order
articles.body: As cases of estranged NRI couples fighting for child custody increasingly result in cross-border litigation, with one spouse getting a favourable order from a foreign court while the other moves an Indian court, Supreme Court has said courts here must make an independent assessment of what is good for the child and the ruling of the foreign court should not be automatically followed, though it must be accorded proper consideration.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again and their adjudication was not easy as they involved deeply emotional and sensitive issues. It added that the welfare of the child “must be understood in the widest sense, not by money or physical comfort alone”.“This position rests on two foundations. The first is that once the court is seized of the matter, it exercises its parens patriae jurisdiction. That jurisdiction obliges it to consider and assess the matter for itself, through the lens of the child’s welfare. The second is that the decision in such cases turns not on the legal rights of the parties but on the welfare of the child. The same emphasis on welfare over legal entitlement runs through our statutes on custody and guardianship. They make clear that a person otherwise entitled to custody or guardianship need not be granted it if that would not be for the welfare of the child. There is thus no ambiguity in the fact that an order of a foreign court must yield to the welfare of the child,” the bench said.“Put differently, a court in this country, when exercising its jurisdiction, cannot blindly follow the order of a foreign court and act merely as an executing court,” the apex court bench said.SC said a parent’s disobedience of a foreign court order did not, by itself, require the Indian court to give automatic effect to that order and also that the paramountcy of the child’s welfare did not mean that the order of the foreign court had to be disregarded. “In deciding what the welfare of the child requires, the court must form its own independent judgement. In doing so, however, it must give proper weight to the order of the foreign court,” the bench said.SC passed the order while directing that a seven-year-old girl, a US citizen, who was brought to India by her mother in breach of a California custody order, return to US.A California court had in 2022 granted the couple joint custody of the child and specifically barred her removal from California without written consent or a court order. In violation of the ruling, the mother left for India with the child after two weeks, leading to the father starting legal proceedings against her in India.SC allowed the petition of the father, who approached the court through advocate Prabhjit Jauhar, against a Karnataka HC order dismissing his plea. After hearing both sides, it said the welfare of the child lay in her continuing to reside in US.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Meet Judah Peake, the 10-year-old from Macclesfield who completed 1,000 press-ups in a month; raised more than £2,500 for charity
articles.summary: Judah Peake, a 10-year-old from Macclesfield, completed a 1,000 press-up fitness challenge in one month and raised more than £2,500 for Tearfund, the
articles.body: Judah Peake, a 10-year-old from Macclesfield, completed a 1,000 press-up fitness challenge in one month and raised more than £2,500 for Tearfund, the international aid and development charity. His sponsored press-up challenge shows how child fundraisers can turn a personal fitness goal into practical charity support, proving that age is no barrier to making a charitable impact. The money supports people affected by disaster, conflict and extreme poverty around the world. The challenge combined fitness training, family encouragement and global giving within a single month. Anyone who would like to support his fundraising can donate online through his JustGiving page.How a festival conversation about Venezuela led Judah to choose Tearfund as his fundraising charityThe idea began during the summer holidays, when Judah and his family were attending a Christian festival. The conversation turned to how they could support people in difficult circumstances around the world, including those affected by the situation in Venezuela. Judah decided he wanted to do something practical about it and chose Tearfund as the recipient. He told Good News Post that his church already works with the charity, which made him want to help too.From a difficult start to a Snowdon summit: How Judah Peake kept his 1,000 press-up challenge goingJudah set himself the task of completing 1,000 press-ups throughout August. He picked the number because it sounded extremely hard, and he admitted he could barely manage them at first, although each day he added more and found it slightly easier. His football coach had also encouraged him to get fitter, so he saw the challenge as a way to reach both goals at once. He kept going wherever he was, including on a family hike to the summit of Snowdon, where he squeezed some in along the way. By the end, he said, he felt a real sense of achievement.How cousins and a doubling pledge from his dad turned Judah's press-ups into a family fundraiserThe fundraiser quickly became a family affair. Judah and his family attend Holy Trinity Church in Hurdsfield, and his cousins joined in and cheered him on throughout the challenge. His father, Robin, 40, told the same publication that the family wants the children to understand that not everyone is born with the same privilege, and to be aware of people in the world who need help. Robin also set an incentive, if Judah reached his £1,000 target, the family would double it. He described the result as amazing.Tearfund praises Judah's commitment and grit and looks ahead to the next challenge he might take onTearfund has publicly praised Judah's effort. Stuart Lee, the charity's fundraising and communications director, told Good News Post that what Judah achieved over the summer showed "such commitment and grit". He added that it is encouraging to see young people who are passionate about fundraising and who think of those with less than themselves, and said he is eager to see which challenge Judah takes on next.You use AI every day. articles.title: From Jan 1, WhatsApp, Telegram won’t work without SIM cards, govt issues guidelines
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India has made SIM binding mandatory from Jan 1, 2027, and the move will mean that messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram will not work
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India has made SIM binding mandatory from Jan 1, 2027, and the move will mean that messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram will not work without a SIM card in the smartphone. The department of telecom has issued guidelines requiring messaging platforms to integrate the accounts with live SIMs used for registration by Dec 31, 2026. If the SIM is removed, replaced or deactivated, the app’s functionality will stop until a valid SIM is reinserted.The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds, phishing, digital arrest scams using Indian mobile numbers and enhance telecom cyber security. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card to abide with the rules. It is learnt Signal has not yet responded to govt notices.From Jan 1, messaging services to be used will have to ensure a registered SIM card is installed in a device. This is likely to impact users of WhatsApp or Telegram over Wi-Fi without registered SIMs. And also those who use more than one device or frequently change their SIM cards.Last Nov, DoT had issued the rules after finding “that some app-based communication services utilising Indian mobile numbers for identification of its customers allows users to consume their services without availability of the underlying subscriber identity module (SIM) within the device in which app-based communication services is running. This feature is being misused to commit cyber-frauds especially from outside the country,” a statement read.To curb this menace, many govt agencies had been asking for SIM binding to be made mandatory. Subsequently, DoT issued directions to major app-based communication services, under the Telecom Cyber Security (TCS) Rules, 2024. These include WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, Arattai, Sharechat, Jiochat and Signal.Now, app-based communication providers will have to ensure that their service is “continuously linked to the SIM card (associated with mobile number used for identification of customers/users or for provisioning or delivery of services) installed in the device, making it impossible to use the app without that specific, active SIM.” And also ensure that “web service instance of the mobile app, if provided, shall be logged out periodically (not later than six hours) and allowing the facility to the user to re-link the device using QR code.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: NYC passes bill to ban horse-drawn carriages, Central Park’s drivers fear for their future
articles.summary: The horse-drawn carriages that have cruised through Central Park for more than 150 years will soon be banished from New York City, ending an iconic tradition beloved by tourists but long opposed by animal welfare activists.
articles.body: The horse-drawn carriages that have cruised through Central Park for more than 150 years will soon be banished from New York City, ending an iconic tradition beloved by tourists but long opposed by animal welfare activists. For the carriage drivers, it’s unclear what comes next. “No one can come up with an appropriate answer because there is none,” said Alexus Lawson, a 28-year-old carriage driver from Queens who grew up with horses and has worked as a riding instructor. Now, she worries about what would become of 7-year-old Starlight and her other horses. “Without a job, how can I take care of my horses?” The New York City Council passed a bill Thursday that would ban horse-drawn carriage rides by June 2028, pulling back the reins after the death of a teenage tourist last spring. But the one question that has come up time and again — what to do with drivers whose jobs would be eliminated — remains largely unanswered. The legislation requires Mayor Zohran Mamdani's office to develop a plan by next April to help the more than 150 remaining drivers find other work. That would include career counseling and referrals for openings in the city's transit, hospitality and taxi industries. It also allows the administration to consider some form of compensation for industry workers. City Hall is working on a detailed plan for the workforce transition and has started discussions on potential compensation, a spokesperson for the mayor said. Mamdani himself has said government has a “civic responsibility to ensure that we are not leaving anybody out to dry.” Carriage drivers wonder about their future Medet Fidan, a former cab driver who traded his steering wheel for a set of reins after ride-hailing apps upended the taxi industry, said he felt like he was being targeted. “I think the city is leaving us a big mess,” said Fidan, 56. “We’re going to lose our businesses, we’re going to lose our jobs, we’re going to lose our livelihoods.” Council Speaker Julie Menin “will remain engaged in the transition process,” a spokesperson said, adding that the legislation seeks to address the longstanding question of what happens to displaced carriage drivers by setting a firm deadline for City Hall to act. “These workers deserve to be protected,” Menin said Thursday, adding that horses no longer have a place among Central Park's pedestrians, cyclists, dog-walkers and gawking tourists. Still, the union representing carriage drivers has vowed to file a legal challenge “the minute the ink dries” on the legislation. Trump opposed the ban, saying a ‘Great Tradition’ will be missed President Donald Trump, whose namesake Trump Tower is a stone's throw from Central Park, bemoaned the ban and called carriage rides “a quintessential New York experience.” “It was a Great Tradition. Another piece of History that’s gone. It will be missed!” Trump wrote on social media. Two of Mamdani's mayoral predecessors had called to end the industry but neither succeeded. Former Mayor Bill de Blasio campaigned on ending the rides on day one of his administration but the effort wilted amid a backlash from unions and a big media blitz involving actor Liam Neeson. Eric Adams, the mayor just before Mamdani, floated a ban late in his term but the proposal went nowhere. Latest push to end the rides began after a tourist's death The latest push began in June after an 18-year-old Indian tourist, Romanch Mahajan, died after jumping from a runaway carriage during a ride. His death appeared to be the first fatality involving a horse carriage in Central Park since the rides began. Mahajan's family has personally appealed to the city to end the rides, offering tearful testimony that they thought the rides were safe. His uncle, Gaurav Mahajan, praised the proposal during a rally Thursday, saying “the hour of justice has finally arrived,” as he stood beside local lawmakers and animal welfare activists. “We're turning our shattering loss into an unbreakable shield of kindness for the city. For months, our family hasn't been allowed to just grieve,” he said. “We've had to fight. We've had to channel our devastating sorrow into a war for change.” Carriage drivers have expressed sympathy for Mahajan and his family but argue that they are being unfairly targeted because of a single accident. “It does nothing for alternate employment, for the continuation of our businesses,” said Christina Hansen, a longtime carriage driver and industry spokesperson. “Who’s going to pay my rent while I’m looking for a job?”

articles.title: Leopard spotted near house in Khudel, forest team launches search
articles.summary: Leopard spotted near a house in Khudel, Indore; forest department launches search, sets trap cameras and cage after reports the animal may be injured.
articles.body: Indore: A leopard was spotted sitting near a house close to Crescent Water Park in Khudel area on Thursday morning, triggering concern among residents of the nearby villages. Locals claimed the animal appeared lethargic and had serious injuries on its head and face.The leopard was seen near the house of farmer Hariom Thakur, who said the animal remained there for some time before fleeing.DFO Sudhakar Singh said the forest department received information around 9.15 am after a villager reported spotting the leopard around 6 am. A rescue team was immediately rushed to the spot and is currently searching the area, but the animal has not been located so far.Singh said trap cameras have been installed and a dog squad also searched the area. A cage has been placed at the site as a precautionary measure, while the rescue team continues to remain in the area.He said the leopard’s injuries have not been independently confirmed by the forest department yet. “From the video, it appears that there is blood on the leopard’s head and mouth, which suggests that it may be injured. Once the search is completed, we will have a clearer picture,” Singh said.Thakur said this was not the first time a leopard had entered the area. On Oct 8, a leopard had allegedly entered his farmhouse and killed livestock. Villagers had then managed to drive the animal away.According to residents, the leopard may have been moving into the habitation from the nearby Ralamandal hills. articles.title: In call with Israeli counterpart, PM Modi says urgent need to restore West Asia peace
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday stressed the urgent need for cessation of hostilities in West Asia in a phone conversation with
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday stressed the urgent need for cessation of hostilities in West Asia in a phone conversation with Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu.The talks took place days before the Israeli general elections, the first since the Oct 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attacks and Israel’s military response. Netanyahu said he invited Modi to light the ceremonial torch alongside Indian pilot Smit Machchhar for Israel’s Independence Day celebrations next year.Machchhar, a pilot for flydubai, sustained injuries during an attack by the Omani co-pilot on a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight on Sept 30. The co-pilot allegedly attempted to take control of the aircraft, following which Machchhar fought him off and managed to unlock the cockpit door.Modi said he had received acall from Netanyahu during which the leaders reviewed the sustained momentum in bilateral ties and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the partnership. Modi did not mention Netanyahu’s invitation in his post on the conversation.“We exchanged views on developments in West Asia and underscored the urgent need to restore peace and stability in the region,” Modi said on X.In his own version of the conversation, Netanyahu did not mention the West Asia situation but said India and Israel were fighting terrorism together. “I spoke with my friend, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and invited him to light the torch alongside a brave Indian pilot on Israel’s Independence Day,” Netanyahu said on X.“Modi thanked me for the invitation and said that on land and in the air, India and Israel are fighting terrorism together. He also commended the strong and decades-old ties between us,” he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
